subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A tensile test on a material is used to determine its:
options: Behaviour under stretching forces, giving yield and ultimate strength
questions.explain: A tensile test applies a pulling force to measure strength, elasticity and elongation.

questions.q: CAM (Computer Aided Manufacture) most directly involves:
options: Using computer-controlled machines such as CNC routers to make parts
questions.explain: CAM uses software to drive CNC machinery that fabricates a designed part.

questions.q: Design for Manufacture (DfM) aims to:
options: Simplify and standardise a design so it is cheaper and easier to produce
Increase the number of unique parts
Make products as complex as possible
questions.explain: DfM optimises a design for efficient, economical and reliable manufacture, often by reducing part count.

questions.q: The 95th percentile is used in anthropometric design when a feature must:
options: Suit the smallest users, e.g. reach distances
Accommodate large users, e.g. doorway or seat clearance
questions.explain: The 95th percentile sizes clearances so that large users are accommodated, e.g. headroom or seat width.

questions.q: The systems approach to manufacturing analyses a process in terms of:
options: Inputs, processes and outputs with feedback
questions.explain: A systems approach models manufacture as inputs, transforming processes and outputs, with feedback for control.

questions.q: Forging improves the strength of a metal component primarily by:
options: Melting and pouring it into a mould
Compressing and deforming the metal to refine and align its grain structure
questions.explain: Forging plastically deforms metal, refining the grain flow to produce a stronger part than casting.

questions.q: Die casting is most appropriate for:
options: High-volume non-ferrous metal parts with good surface finish
questions.explain: Die casting injects molten non-ferrous metal into reusable steel dies for high-volume accurate parts.

questions.q: Art Deco design, popular in the 1920s-30s, is characterised by:
options: Sleek geometric forms, symmetry and luxurious decorative detail
questions.explain: Art Deco combined streamlined geometric forms with rich materials and decorative elegance.

questions.q: MDF is an engineered board that is manufactured by:
options: Gluing thin veneers at right angles
Bonding fine wood fibres with resin under heat and pressure
questions.explain: Medium-density fibreboard is made from compressed wood fibres and resin, giving a smooth uniform board.

questions.q: Ethical sourcing of timber is supported by certification from:
questions.explain: The FSC certifies that timber comes from responsibly managed, sustainable forests.

questions.q: Consumer protection legislation (e.g. the Consumer Rights Act) requires goods to be:
options: Of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described
questions.explain: Consumer law requires that goods are of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and match their description.

questions.q: Inclusive (universal) design aims to create products that are:
options: Usable only by the average person
Usable by the widest possible range of people regardless of age or ability
As cheap as possible regardless of usability
questions.explain: Inclusive design seeks to make products accessible to as many users as possible, including those with disabilities.

questions.q: Anthropometric data is used in design and is typically expressed using:
questions.explain: Anthropometrics presents body measurement ranges as percentiles to size products for target users.

questions.q: New and emerging technologies such as automation can impact employment by:
options: Reducing some routine manual roles while creating demand for new technical skills
Eliminating the need for any human input ever
Having no effect on the workforce
questions.explain: Automation displaces routine tasks but generates new roles requiring different, often higher, technical skills.

questions.q: Vacuum forming is a process in which a heated thermoplastic sheet is:
options: Drawn over a mould by removing the air beneath it
Forced into a mould under high injection pressure
questions.explain: Vacuum forming sucks air from beneath a softened sheet so atmospheric pressure pulls it onto the mould.

questions.q: In additive manufacturing (FDM 3D printing), the object is created by:
options: Building up material layer by layer from a digital model
Drawing material through a heated die
Removing material from a solid block
questions.explain: Additive manufacturing deposits successive layers of material guided by a CAD/STL model.

questions.q: Designing a product to be repairable rather than disposable primarily supports which of the 6 Rs?
questions.explain: Making products serviceable and fixable embodies the 'Repair' principle, extending useful life.

questions.q: Lamination (as in plywood) increases strength by:
options: Bonding layers with the grain alternating in direction
questions.explain: Plywood layers veneers with alternating grain direction, distributing stress and resisting warping.

questions.q: Which property describes a material's ability to be drawn into a wire?
questions.explain: Ductility is the ability to undergo tensile deformation, such as being drawn into wire, without fracturing.

questions.q: User-centred design (UCD) places at the heart of the process:
options: The needs, wants and limitations of the end user
questions.explain: UCD continuously involves and prioritises the end user throughout the design process.

questions.q: Which scale of production best describes a bespoke piece of furniture made to a unique client order?
questions.explain: A single bespoke item made to order is one-off or job production.

questions.q: Which manufacturing process is most suited to producing large quantities of identical thermoplastic parts such as bottle caps?
questions.explain: Injection moulding forces molten thermoplastic into a mould at high speed, ideal for high-volume identical parts.

questions.q: Which process is used to manufacture hollow thin-walled plastic products like detergent bottles?
questions.explain: Blow moulding inflates a heated parison against a mould to form hollow thin-walled containers.

questions.q: A primary aim of designing to reduce material use ('Reduce' in the 6 Rs) is to:
options: Use fewer resources and less energy, lowering environmental impact
questions.explain: Reducing material and energy use lowers resource depletion, cost and environmental impact.

questions.q: Quantum Tunnelling Composite (QTC) is a smart material whose electrical resistance:
options: Decreases sharply when compressed or deformed
questions.explain: QTC changes from an insulator to a conductor as pressure brings conductive particles closer together.

questions.q: Which testing method assesses a material's resistance to a sudden impact load?
questions.explain: Charpy and Izod tests strike a notched specimen to measure energy absorbed, indicating toughness.

questions.q: Design for Disassembly (DfD) primarily supports sustainability by:
options: Enabling components to be easily separated for repair, reuse or recycling
Reducing the number of recyclable materials used
Making products impossible to take apart
questions.explain: DfD allows easy separation of parts and materials at end-of-life for recovery and recycling.

questions.q: Dieter Rams, associated with Braun, is best known for the design philosophy:
questions.explain: Dieter Rams championed minimalist functional design summarised as 'less, but better'.

questions.q: The work of contemporary studio Dyson is most associated with:
options: Technology-led innovation such as bagless cyclonic vacuum cleaners
questions.explain: Dyson is known for engineering-driven innovation, notably cyclonic separation in bagless vacuum cleaners.

questions.q: The British Standards Institution (BSI) Kitemark indicates that a product:
options: Has been independently tested to meet a recognised standard of safety/quality
questions.explain: The Kitemark is a BSI certification mark showing a product meets a defined standard.
